scope: Focused full mathematical/source-contract review of JRP1–JRP5, including the literal auxiliary-place inertia producer. JRP6–JRP15 are outside this focused review.
findings: JRP1 uses the actual original Coef subalgebra: its DVR and finite Z_ell-module fields imply it is the integer ring of the finite coefficient fraction field. Completeness and finite residue field follow, and successive simple-root lifting gives the multiplicative Teichmuller section with exactly the source exponent card(k)-1. The original coefficient ring is not replaced.

JRP2 proves maximal-ideal elements map to norm strictly below1 without assuming continuity of the point. The reciprocal-integrality monic equation gives a unit in the source local ring killed by the point if the norm were at least1. IsCO.res_surj then gives the exact prescribed residue map under every finite coefficient extension used to contain a particular value. No common finite field for the entire algebraic point is required.

JRP3 is the prime-to-p finite inertia character law. The fixed field of the open character kernel supplies a faithful finite group of distinct field automorphisms; their independence produces the nonzero eigenvector. The norm-one quotient of this vector and its conjugate has inertia-trivial reduction, and prime-to-p roots reduce injectively. This proves the precise cyclotomic conjugation identity, including for open subgroups and residue prime3.

JRP4 correctly raises an arbitrary residual scalar characteristic-polynomial matrix to ell-powers. The Cayley-Hamilton/binomial estimate has a uniform finite-level exponent for every rank. At each finite level inertia is an ell-group. A nontrivial character of this group contradicts JRP3 after a scalar power of the chosen cyclotomic-nontrivial element; its residual cyclotomic value remains nontrivial because an ell-power is injective on the finite residue field. Separation proves original inertia triviality, without semisimplicity or a rank bound.

JRP5 applies inherited ADK1 only to the compact local decomposition representation. A bounded orbit of the standard lattice gives an actual stable free O-prime lattice. Conjugation preserves characteristic polynomials, and JRP2 together with Pair.red identifies their residues with the original Dbar. The concrete Hida-setting decomposition group embeds openly in G_Qp; the original splitting condition supplies its map to the same G0 with exact D0 and I0 images and cyclotomic character. All three literal V0ok clauses therefore feed JRP4, proving the complete original auxiliary-place endpoint for every continuous point representation of positive rank.
exact_scope_retained: Actual original coefficient object, residual map, universal determinant, Hida frame, quotient and auxiliary place.
Prime p differs from ell as in the original Hida setting; no new rank or prime bound.
No semisimplicity of either the global representation or its local restriction.
Only the inertia component of original v0b is needed and reconstructed here; no claim about its separate twisted-commutant conclusion.
The finite-coefficient lemma ADK1 is an inherited, previously reviewed human result.
not_claimed: Closure of an entire remaining RH/GRH obligation
